description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

phases.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
phases.notes: Per analyses 032 + 035: Tweedles are 78.8% of total run cost, with ~13-15 calls per deliberation reflecting heavy write_file → run_tests → write_file tool loops. Two batched fixes: (1) surface tool calls on the bus event log so post-run analysis can quantify exactly which tool calls drive cost (currently inferred via per-agent telemetry); (2) diff-based write tool that lets agents send deltas instead of full file contents, with analysis 032 estimating ~3.5× cost compression on iterative file authoring. Sequencing: surface first so we can measure baseline tool-call distribution; then diff tool with measurements to verify the predicted compression. After both ship, second pass to identify other easy cost/clock wins from whatever the surfaced data reveals.

phases.title: Polish: ambient liveness, first-use UX, small ergonomic improvements after P11
Feature lifecycle + workflow composability: split design / implement / verify; operator batching
Cross-run stability: make iterating tdd-design + tdd-implement against the same project the expected mode of operation
phases.notes: Most observed failure modes from multi-pass obol runs land as either 'everything completed at $0' (cross-run seeds re-emitted as fresh work) or duplicate artifacts (Rabbit revising mid-meeting, M2/M3 source-set sprawl). P12 shipped piecemeal patches (per-thread cost f36bbf7, exit_condition is_seed filter v0.3.2, consumed_by binding fb4fc0e); P13 closes the remaining gaps so cross-run iteration is the workflow's expected economic shape.

phases.title: Discovery: requirements gathering as a first-class phase
phases.notes: New Interview abstraction (sibling to Meeting), three focused interviews (Alice/Cat/Rabbit) that capture operator intent as structured requirement artifacts before any design work. Optional — projects can still skip straight to tdd-design. Backfill workflow lets existing projects catch up. This is the structural layer that lets Wonderland be a long-running collaboration tool instead of a series of one-shot generation passes — see project_interviews_milestones_thesis.md. Milestones layer follows in a subsequent phase, shape TBD based on what the requirement-artifact corpus looks like in practice.

phases.title: Milestones: sequential ordering above features
phases.notes: Adds the layer between requirements and features. Three-agent planning meeting (Rabbit + Cat + Alice) groups requirements into ordered milestones; tdd-design runs scoped to a milestone; dashboard surfaces milestone progression as the operator's primary attention surface. Cross-run continuity: re-running milestone-plan after a follow-up discovery reads the existing plan + new requirements and amends or appends as makes sense (registry updates by slug match). Status derived from features-belonging-to-milestone (no separate lifecycle log in v1).

phases.title: Local inference: bring-your-own-model
phases.notes: Add OpenAI-compatible model provider support (ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, plus actual OpenAI / Together / Groq) alongside the Anthropic backend. Per-agent model selection so senior agents (Caterpillar, Cheshire Cat) run on premium while executors (Tweedles, Hatter) run on cheap local. Operator can run the substrate without an Anthropic key, accepting degraded performance. Sequencing: T-l1 unblocks everything (must be first); T-l2 → T-l3 is the OpenAI-compat adapter critical path; T-l4 + T-l5 parallelize once T-l1 lands; T-l6 sits on T-l4; T-l7 (pilot) sits on T-l2+l3+l4 landing; T-l8 (docs) reflects T-l7 findings. The hard part is quality cliff not architecture — Llama 3.2 3B vs Haiku 4.5 at constitutional adherence, JSON output reliability, tool-use reliability, multi-step reasoning. Phase exit: a pilot of hello-endpoint against Llama 3.2 via ollama produces an artifact, failure modes catalogued for a follow-up phase. Deferred to future work: prompt-cache equivalence beyond provider defaults; degraded-mode workflow variants (depend on T-l7 findings).

phases.title: GUID-everywhere: stable artifact identity
phases.notes: Replace slug-as-identity with GUID-as-identity across every artifact registry. Slug becomes cosmetic (human readability, dashboard display); GUID becomes load-bearing (routing, dedup, cross-references, source resolution). The slug-as-identity model has been the root cause of the entire failure-mode family we've been patching all night: phantom-slug citations (Rabbit inventing slugs that don't resolve), slug drift across rotations (same concept, near-duplicate slugs all hashed differently), attribution drift (tickets citing story-X that doesn't exist), feature-level near-duplicates (9 features for 3 concepts because each iteration coined slightly different slugs). Constitutional tightening at the agent layer is a band-aid; substrate-level identity stability is the durable fix. Sequencing: T-g1 (payload field) unblocks everything; T-g2 (registry layer) + T-g3 (filenames) are critical-path; T-g4 (bus + cross-refs) + T-g5 (source resolution) ship together once registries are GUID-aware; T-g6 (agent protocols) teaches the team to use GUIDs; T-g7 (UI) is the last consumer to update; T-g8 (back-compat) lets prior pilots keep working without manual migration; T-g9 closes the loop with a fresh end-to-end pilot. ~1-2 days focused work. Expected outcome: phantom-slug and slug-drift classes of bug become substrate-impossible; semantic-duplication (9 features for 3 concepts) remains a constitutional discipline problem but loses the substrate's contribution to making it worse.

phases.title: Existing-project onramp: Holmes + Watson archaeology for codebases that already exist
phases.notes: Make Wonderland droppable into existing codebases. Today the substrate assumes greenfield (discovery interview → milestones → design → build from zero); this phase adds the onramp where the operator points Wonderland at a populated repo, agents derive structural understanding from the code, and the trajectory picks up at 'we're at milestone N, design N+1.' Phase exit: Wonderland-developing-Wonderland is the validation pilot — Wonderland-the-system designs and implements a Wonderland feature, with the diff and $ spend reported. Casting decision (resolved): Holmes is the archaeologist — the great detective plumbing the depths of an unknown codebase, deducing structure from fragmentary evidence (Holmes:codebase :: Sherlock:crime scene). Characteristic failure mode: over-confident deduction, narrative-fitting to messy code. Watson is the chronicler / operator-facing voice that translates Holmes's deductions into artifacts and questions the operator can act on (Watson:Holmes :: Alice:Rabbit). Incident + security framings (the original 2b405ec6 scoping) become fast-follow workflows that reuse the same constitutions. Sequencing: existing-state artifact kinds (existing_module / existing_capability / existing_pattern) land first to define the vocabulary; codebase exploration tools ship in parallel (file traversal, dependency probes, structural inspection beyond the current verify_imports); Holmes + Watson constitutions get authored alongside the archaeology decision mode + allowed_decisions guardrail; discovery-existing.yaml composes the above into a runnable workflow; current-state milestone seed lets the operator mark where the existing code sits on the trajectory; finally the self-developing pilot closes the loop.

phases.title: Tier 2 autonomous pilot: end-to-end Wonderland with operator as gate-approver only
phases.notes: Validation goal: a fresh greenfield project completes end-to-end (discovery → milestone-plan → tdd-design × N → tdd-implement × N → working app) with operator participating ONLY as gate-approver — no hand-edits to artifacts, no killing wedged runs, no manual state cleanup. Paper-grade evidence: 'Wonderland produces a working app autonomously on Haiku-4.5 for $X in Y minutes.' Sequencing: M1-deletion bug (08e60dd0) is the highest-risk untraced data-loss path and must be fixed first; convergence-failure detection (73690727) and env-class verify routing (dc95169a) prevent the two highest-leverage wedge classes; cross-feature ticket consolidation (24d57b85) and milestone-vs-code coherence (eb138e74) are nice-to-haves that improve quality but aren't strictly required for the autonomous demonstration. Once the prerequisites land, fire 040f2f3f as the validation pilot. Phase exit: a Tier 2 pilot completes with the working-app artifact + total spend reported + the intervention-point measurement (where, if anywhere, operator action was needed).

activePhase.title: Tier 2 autonomous pilot: end-to-end Wonderland with operator as gate-approver only
activePhase.goal: Get Wonderland to Tier 2 autonomy: a fresh pilot completes end-to-end with operator participating ONLY as gate-approver. No hand-edits, no killing wedged runs, no manual cleanup. Paper-grade evidence: 'Wonderland produces a working app autonomously on Haiku-4.5 for $X in Y minutes.'
activePhase.sequencing: T-a1 (M1-deletion trace) first — highest-risk untraced data-loss path. T-a2 (branching memory) is the architectural heavy-lift but unblocks the whole class of memory-bleed wedges that required operator surgery in mvp-demo. T-a3 + T-a4 (convergence-failure + env-class routing) are smaller substrate primitives that prevent the next two highest-leverage wedge classes; can parallelize. T-a5 + T-a6 (cross-feature consolidation + milestone-vs-code coherence) are nice-to-haves that improve quality but aren't strictly required for the autonomous demonstration. T-a7 is the pilot itself — fires once T-a1 through T-a4 land.

tasks.title: Trace + fix M1 milestone deletion path
tasks.details: 08e60dd0 — Add tracing wrapper to MilestoneRegistry that logs every unlink with stack trace; reproduce M1 deletion in a fresh mvp-style pilot to capture the actual code path. Likely suspects: phased snapshot firing on a phase boundary we missed, retract handler unlinking on a non-ticket target_kind, MilestoneRegistry.write() rename path firing with payload-guid-matches-different-slug. Blocks T-a7 — recurring data loss is incompatible with Tier 2 autonomy.

tasks.title: Branch episodic memory at the design level
tasks.details: e2d44cac — supersedes c54056b7. Each milestone's design pass gets its own branch of episodic memory rooted at a clean snapshot (the project's 'milestone N-1 closed' summary). Implementation passes branch from their milestone's design branch, per-feature inside that. On milestone closed, Mock Turtle generates a 'milestone N summary' artifact at project-level layer — captures conclusions without deliberation. Future branches read the summary but never inherit per-milestone argument noise. Eliminates the operator-surgery class of failures entirely. Probably the single most leveraged item on this phase.
tasks.resolution: Chunks A+B+C shipped: schema v2 + branch contextvar + runner wiring + consolidation orchestrator + Mock Turtle attribution + dashboard hook. 411 tests pass (11 new). Memory branches scope per-milestone; consolidation fires on last-feature-verified; design churn no longer cross-bleeds.

tasks.title: Convergence-failure detection
tasks.details: 73690727 — Detect when the same finding-cluster recurs across N consecutive review passes on the same feature. Emit a 'spec_ambiguity' observation flagging the contract artifact(s) the findings cite, pause the implementation loop pending operator disambiguation. Stops cost-burn on convergence failures (mvp-demo F1 burned 5+ passes oscillating on DELETE shape) and gives the operator a clear signal where to intervene.
tasks.resolution: Convergence-failure detection shipped: fingerprint = (file_loc_no_lines, normalized_concern). Detects when same fingerprint recurs in N consecutive review passes (default N=3). On detect, persists spec_ambiguity artifact at .wonderland/spec-ambiguity/, extracts cited contract/ADR references for operator attention. 10 tests, integrated into _route_blocking_review path. Build_check path opts out (auto_complete_in_flight_tickets=False sentinel).

tasks.title: Env-class verify-failure routing
tasks.details: dc95169a — Detect environment-class verify failures (ModuleNotFoundError from missing pyproject deps, missing env vars, missing migrations, broken venv) and route to operator-attention instead of synthesizing implementation tickets the Tweedles can't honestly do. Stops the budget-burning loop where Tweedles correctly refuse env work and hit MEETING_BUDGET.
tasks.resolution: Env-class verify-failure routing shipped: classifier with 7 patterns (ModuleNotFoundError, npm ERR, pytest cannot collect, etc.), partition + operator_attention artifact at .wonderland/operator-attention/, suggested commands (uv add, npm install). Build_check path wires through route_verify_findings — code-class findings still synthesize Tweedle tickets, env-class skip ticket synthesis and write artifact for operator. 12 tests; mvp-demo F2 wedge structurally prevented.

tasks.title: Cross-feature ticket consolidation (M3.75)
tasks.details: 24d57b85 — After all per-feature M3.5 instances complete, run a cross-feature consolidation pass that identifies near-duplicate tickets across features (same source requirements, similar slugs, overlapping descriptions) and consolidates to one ticket under the most-fitting feature. Improves ticket quality but not strictly required for autonomy.
tasks.resolution: Cross-feature ticket consolidation shipped as wonderland.cross_feature module. Detection: cluster tickets by upstream-source frozenset (excluding parent feature); flag clusters with >=2 distinct parent features. Best-home selection: Jaccard similarity between cluster's upstream sources and each candidate parent feature's sources, tie-break alphabetical slug for determinism. Apply: walk retracted tickets through lifecycle to ABORTED state, leave files on disk for forensics. 9 tests. Currently exposed as callable; tdd-design.yaml phase wiring for auto-fire is a small follow-up.

tasks.title: Milestone-vs-code coherence review
tasks.details: eb138e74 — M8 review catches code-vs-ticket drift but not code-vs-milestone-spec drift. Add a 'milestone_satisfaction' build_check that diffs current code state against the active milestone's done_when bullets. Could run as part of M9 verify. Improves quality but not strictly required for autonomy.

tasks.title: Tier 2 autonomous pilot — validation
tasks.details: 040f2f3f — Fresh greenfield project, end-to-end (discovery → milestone-plan → tdd-design × N → tdd-implement × N → working demo) with operator participating only as gate-approver. No hand-edits to artifacts, no killing wedged runs, no manual cleanup. Phase exit: working-app artifact + total spend reported + the intervention-point measurement (where, if anywhere, operator action was needed). Fires once T-a1 through T-a4 land; T-a5 + T-a6 nice-to-haves can land before or after.
tasks.resolution: Mvp-demo2 pilot completed end-to-end. Working full-stack notebook app shipped for $83.78 across 3 milestones. Operator participated primarily as gate-approver: skipped duplicate features at multiple points, ticket-level scope filtering on M3 megalith. One Tier 2 violation: mid-pilot substrate fix shipped (auto-directive synthesis + seed-fallback scoping). Zero killed runs, zero memory surgery, zero hand-edited artifacts. 7 substrate roadmap items surfaced for follow-up. Paper's Wright Brothers moment captured in project_first_tier2_pilot_completion.md.
